question.problem:
Consider the function $f:R\to {R}^{2},$ defined by 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:R\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a scalar $x$ is the column vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} \\ ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂x}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times 1}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a scalar $x\in R,$ and

- outputs a vector $f(x)\in {R}^{2}$ defined by 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{2\times 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the total derivative at $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and get

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\pi }{2})=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
